extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to the Notices of the American Mathematical Society
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting articles, graphics, permissions, and ancillary materials for publication in the Notices of the AMS. Includes audience/tonal expectations, length/reference limits by article type, refereeing policy, graphics technical specs, and documentation/permission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Research articles should be written to be understandable by, and interesting to, a variety of readers: good second-year mathematics graduate students, academic mathematicians in fields outside of your own, mathematically focused researchers in fields such as economics and physics, mathematicians working in industry, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know what you want to say, understand the audience, think clearly, and polish the draft repeatedly. Use accessible exposition appropriate for non-specialist mathematicians; consult guides such as N. Higham and S. Krantz on mathematical writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone for professional and social-issues articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles concerning professional and social issues should be interesting to a substantial fraction of the AMS membership, and written in a scholarly tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inflammatory language, sweeping generalizations unsupported by evidence, or personal attacks. Well-argued and respectfully presented opinions on important issues that some may find controversial are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of exposition and polish
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles should be written to a high standard of exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a page budget and limited referee time; the editors will spend resources only on high-quality articles with lasting value. Authors are expected to revise and polish drafts repeatedly before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refereeing and publication conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles are refereed for exposition and correctness, and publication is contingent on authors making the changes requested by the referees and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters to the Editor are generally not refereed, but the Editor-in-Chief reserves the right to negotiate changes (e.g., shortening) with the author before publication, and not to print anything that is well beyond the limits of normal professional discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page and reference limits by article type
rubrics_metrics.description: Usual upper bounds on length and references (for LaTeX use the Notices style file; for WYSIWYG assume ~650 words/page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature articles: 10 pages, 20 references. Memorial and history articles: 10 pages, 20 references. All other articles: 10 pages, 15 references. Editors may impose smaller upper bounds for certain types of articles, and may impose lower bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: No abstract or biography
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles may not include an abstract or a biography of the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: References format and MR numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: References should be in the form illustrated in the style file and, in particular, should include MR numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Notices style file examples for consistent formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript will be submitted as a single PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the separate Submissions Checklist to ensure completeness of your submission, because a submission includes more than just a manuscript of an article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission checklist: required items
rubrics_metrics.description: Items required with submission (completeness checklist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: PDF of manuscript including all graphics/photos; captions for all graphics and photos; permissions for each graphics image/photo/headshot and (for Feature article) opener; identifier for each author in the form 'Jane Doe is a professor of mathematics at Academia College. Her email address is jdoe@academia.edu'; headshot for each author; if Feature article: a horizontally oriented opener image. Ensure permissions documentation is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions: authors' responsibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for obtaining permission to use any images or text quotations included in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissions must be obtained prior to final submission and permission documentation must be provided to avoid delays or omission of material. Authors are responsible for payment of any fees charged by the copyright holder. Permissions must be free of restrictions that limit the AMS’s ability to produce, publish, promote, and distribute worldwide in print and electronic formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: When written permission is required
rubrics_metrics.description: Written permission will be required if you are using any of your own material that has been previously published, are using another person's work (including graphics) whether or not previously published, or are including photographs you did not take or do not own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for permissions documentation (third-party permissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures/graphics/photos/images/text not created by or owned by the author(s), provide specific documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documentation: (1) Contact info — name and email (or phone) of copyright owner; (2) Proof of permission — written correspondence clearly indicating Notices of the AMS has been granted permission to publish/reprint worldwide in print and electronic formats without restrictions; (3) Source documentation — full citations for all third-party material, including public domain and Creative Commons content (with links); (4) Credit lines — indicate any specific credit lines desired; if none, AMS will use 'Courtesy of {Name of Copyright Owner}'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample permission-request text
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested wording to request permission from a rights holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include title of article, note acceptance for publication in Notices, attach copy of requested content, ask for confirmation that the requester is the copyright holder and that permission is granted worldwide in print and electronic formats; ask for any requested credit line. Attach the requested content to the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting policy / author distribution rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may freely post their article on their own website, institutional repository, and arXiv.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you post a version with more references than those allowed by the Notices, include a note: 'This is the author's version of an article from the Notices of the AMS with an expanded reference list'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: identify raster vs vector
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should identify whether a graphic is raster or vector to determine suitability for print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raster graphics are pixel arrays (photographs, Photoshop, Paint programs). Vector graphics are created with vector illustration programs and scale without loss of quality (Adobe Illustrator, Inkscape, Mathematica, Matlab).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: size and resolution specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices graphics are typically formatted in two sizes: 1 column (small) and 2 column (large); provide minimum pixel dimensions and DPI requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small (1-column) printed at 3-7/16 inches wide — photographic original: at least 1031 pixels wide; large (2-column) printed at 7-1/8 inches wide — photographic original: at least 2138 pixels wide. Raster (Photographic Images): 300 pixels per inch required. Raster (Line Art Images): 600 pixels per inch required; for line art, small original at least 2062 pixels wide and large original at least 4276 pixels wide. (Follow the graphics guidelines and check actual pixel/dimension values before submission.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector graphics considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector graphics yield high resolution but may have other printing issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most common problem is that line weights are too thin to print. Ensure line weights are sufficiently thick for print (see font size / line weight minima).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic detail requirements: fonts and line weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure fonts and line weights in figures are legible and strong for print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum printable font size is 6 pt. Minimum line width is 0.5 (units implied). Fonts should be embedded in figures rather than superimposed on figures using TeX commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted file formats for graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Most standard file formats can be used for figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable formats include JPEG, TIFF, EPS, PNG, GIF, and PDF. For LaTeX submissions, include the images; for WYSIWYG, identify filenames and placement in manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to check image dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: A quick method to find whether your image meets pixel/dimension requirements using a web browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open the image in a browser, right-click and view image info or open in new tab; dimensions appear in the header/tab or popup dialog (procedures differ slightly by browser: Safari, Firefox, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opener image requirement for Feature articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature article submissions require a horizontally oriented image to be used as an opener.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opener could be one of your figures, another image you created, or a free image taken from elsewhere. Ensure permissions and that the image meets size/resolution requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit line handling and defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should indicate specific credit lines wanted for third-party material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no credit line is specified, AMS will use 'Courtesy of {Name of Copyright Owner}'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party material from AMS publications
rubrics_metrics.description: If using third-party material that originally appeared in an AMS publication, additional steps are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact reprint-permission@ams.org to confirm that AMS can grant reuse rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact points for graphics and permissions questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated AMS contacts for graphics and permissions inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphics questions: ga-request@ams.org. Permissions questions: Karen Wargo (kxw@ams.org). For reprint-permission related to AMS publications: reprint-permission@ams.org.
